title: Wonton Soup
subtitle: Pork-filled dumplings in clear chicken broth
excerpt: Small pork and ginger dumplings made in gyoza wrappers and simmered in a clean, well-seasoned chicken broth with pak choi. Folding wontons is easier than it looks; the method below describes the simplest fold. The filling takes 5 minutes to mix and the wontons cook in the broth in 4 to 5 minutes.
sourceNotes: Wonton soup is a Cantonese staple with origins in southern China; the word 'wonton' translates roughly to 'swallowing clouds' in Cantonese, a reference to the dumpling's billowing shape when floating in broth.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shaped, uncooked wontons can be placed on a floured tray, covered and refrigerated for up to 4 hours before cooking.

content.text: Gyoza wrappers work well here; square wonton wrappers are traditional but round gyoza wrappers fold just as easily. To fold the simplest wonton: place a teaspoon of filling in the centre of a wrapper, fold it in half into a half-moon, press to seal, then bring the two corners together and press to join. This gives a bonnet shape that holds together well during cooking. Wet your finger with water and run it around the edge before folding to help the wrapper seal.

items.prepNote: square wonton wrappers are traditional; round gyoza wrappers work equally well

content.text: Make the filling: combine the pork mince, finely chopped spring onion, grated ginger, soy sauce and sesame oil in a bowl. Mix well with a fork until the mixture is uniform and slightly sticky. Season with a small pinch of salt (the soy already adds salt, so taste first).

Fill and fold the wontons: place a wrapper on a clean surface. Put 1 heaped teaspoon of filling in the centre. Wet the edges with a damp finger, fold in half and press firmly to seal. Bring the two sealed corners around and press together to form a bonnet shape. Place on a lightly floured tray. Repeat until all the filling is used.
Bring the chicken stock to a simmer in a large saucepan. Taste the stock and season if needed; the wontons are salty so the broth should be lightly seasoned.

Add the wontons to the simmering stock in two or three batches to avoid crowding. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until they float to the surface and the wrappers are translucent. Add the pak choi in the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Ladle the wontons, pak choi and hot broth into deep bowls. Scatter with finely chopped chives and serve immediately.

items.symptom: Wontons are breaking apart in the broth
items.cause: The edges were not sealed firmly enough or the broth was boiling too vigorously
items.fix: Simmer rather than boil; a gentle simmer holds wontons intact. Next time press the sealed edges firmly and double-check for gaps before cooking.

items.symptom: Filling is still pink inside after 5 minutes
items.cause: Wontons were too large or the broth was not hot enough
items.fix: Cut open a wonton to check; if pink, continue simmering for another 2 minutes. Next time use no more than 1 heaped teaspoon of filling per wrapper.
